SUBJECT:  RECEIVE AND FILE THE MONTHLY INVESTMENT ACTIVITY
  REPORT FOR MAY 2021.

ISSUE
Receive and file the monthly investment activity report for May 2021.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council accept the monthly and quarterly investment
activity reports for City of Palmdale and Successor Agency for May 2021.

BACKGROUND
Pursuant to Section 16 of the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency Investment
Policy, the City Treasurer shall prepare and present monthly and quarterly reports on
investments to the City Manager/Executive Director and the City Council/Directors. The
reports shall detail the type of investment, name of the issuer, purchase date, date of
maturity, amount of deposit, and rate of interest. This information shall be provided for
all City and Successor Agency pooled investments, as well as for Certificates of
Participation, Revenue Bonds, Tax Allocation Bonds, Assessment Districts and
Community Facilities District accounts which are managed by outside Fiscal Agents.

The monthly report provides a synopsis of the investment activity for the City of Palmdale
and Successor Agency. The reports provide information on assets, allocations, average
maturities, yields, and book valuations.

The market values presented for pooled City and Successor Agency investments are
based on closing prices for the related investment as of the date of this report. This
information was obtained from the Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg Financial Markets,
Capital Market Finances, or other reliable source of market prices.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
July 13, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
Compliance with Investment Policy

For April, the invested portfolio amount for the City of Palmdale totaled $188,594,123
an increase of $4,523,580 from the previous month and a decrease of $13,426,454
increase in comparison to last year. The increase in overall portfolio balance from the
previous month is a result of investment maturities and interest received during the
current period.

The par value of Successor Agency’s portfolio as of April, was $11,347,889. The balance
increased by $10,204 from last month due to interest received.

All investments meet criteria appropriate to Section 8 of the Investment Policy. The
portfolios are based on a combination of various investments, including CDs, Corporate
Notes, U.S. Treasury Securities and Government Agency Paper, each adhering to
portfolio percentage limitations.

The Finance Division is the custodian for the City and Successor Agency’s investment
portfolio and follows the three main principles of both entity’s investment policy to 1.)
Investment in financial instruments that mitigate the risk of monetary losses stemming
from market fluctuations, 2.) Establish and maintain a portfolio that has sufficient liquidity
to allow the City and Successor Agency to meet all anticipated cash requirements, and
3.) Seek out investment instruments that provide a competitive market rate of return.

Liquidity

One core approach the Finance Division focuses on, is providing liquidity to measure up
to the City and Successor Agency’s operational requirements. Thus, the Finance
Department is currently investing in two pooled funds, LAIF and CAMP. These are
intended for the daily operational activities, used for economic uncertainties and
maintenance needs. The pooled funds provide a higher liquidity ratio to ensure the City
and Successor Agency meet cash flow requirements.

Total LAIF balance for the City of Palmdale is $123,980,705, with no change from the
prior month.

Successor Agency LAIF balance at the end of May was $5,187,677, a 29.5 percent
decrease from June, but flat to the prior month. The decrease in balance for the year is
due to withdraws to cover monthly expenses and debt service payments.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
July 13, 2021

CAMP’s balance for City of Palmdale is $248,662, compared to April’s balance of
$248,650.

The interest rates presented are the most current rates available as of the date of this
report. As of May 31, 2021, the interest rates for LAIF and CAMP investments were at
.32 percent and .05 percent, respectively. By comparison, the LAIF and CAMP interest
rates at the end of March were at .34 percent and .06 percent. Both rates have been
steadily declining. This time last year, LAIF and CAMP rates were at 1.36 percent and
0.67, respectively.

The chart above shows both the Local Agency Investment Fund and California
Management Program’s average monthly yields from the beginning of FY 2021, the
graph depicts the prolonged period of declining rates.

We anticipate a further decrease in the upcoming months, considering the economic
impacts of COVID. Overall, LAIF shows better performance than CAMP in interest rates.
The difference between the performance of the two funds is partly due to the varying
pool characteristics. CAMP’s portfolio composition is much more subject to market
volatility, resulting in performance variation.

Diversity

The Finance Division aims to diversify the investment portfolios to avoid incurring
unreasonable and avoidable risks regarding specific security types or individual financial
institutions.

City of Palmdale and Successor Agency’s investment portfolios remain strongly
diversified. The monthly and quarterly reports include all investments held by both
entities and current book values as of May 31, 2021.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Monthly Report on Investments
July 13, 2021

In May, there were two Government Agency Papers acquired two U.S. Treasury Notes
acquired. One U.S. Treasury Note and one Government Agency Paper matured at a
combined loss of $60,675. No other securities were called or matured.
It is anticipated that both the City of Palmdale and Successor Agency will have sufficient
moneys to meet its expenditure requirements for the next six months as we continue to
monitor any financial impact due to the Coronavirus pandemic.
Attached are summaries of the investments on the City of Palmdale and Successor

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-065 a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale designating by title and name those officials who are authorized to sign checks
and warrants and repeal Resolution No. CC 2020-029.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-065 designating
by title and name those officials who are authorized to sign checks and warrants, and
repeal Resolution No. CC 2020-029.

DISCUSSION
Resolution No. CC 2021-065 will reflect the hiring, appointment, or deletion of the following, and
add or delete him or her as an authorized signer of checks and warrants for the City.

Richard Loa, Mayor Pro Tem – Deleting
Laura Bettencourt, Mayor Pro Tem - Adding
Janelle Samson, Assistant Finance Manager – Adding
Janelle Samson, Deputy City Treasurer – Adding

There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-064 a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale establishing an appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2021-22 pursuant to Article
XIII B of the California Constitution and repeal Resolution No. CC 2020-053.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-064 to establish
a new appropriations limit for Fiscal Year 2021-22 pursuant to Article XIII B of the
Constitution of the State of California and repeal Resolution No. CC 2020-053.

BACKGROUND
Article XIIIB of the California State Constitution, more commonly referred to as the Gann
Initiative or Gann Appropriations Limit, was adopted by California voters in 1980. The
Gann Appropriations Limit places restrictions on the amount of tax proceeds that state
and local governmental agencies can receive and appropriate each fiscal year.

The Limit changes each fiscal year and is different for each governmental agency. The
Limit is calculated based on the actual amount of tax proceeds appropriated during the
1978-79 fiscal year and is increased each year for inflation and population growth.
Inflationary adjustments are, by law, based on the growth in the California Per Capita
Income or the growth in non-residential assessed valuation due to new construction within
the City. Population adjustments are based on the population growth of the City or the
population growth within the City's county. The decision as to which of the options to
select is made annually by a recorded vote of the City Council.

The statutes regarding the adoption of the Appropriations Limit, contained in
Government Code Section 7910, require the governing body to annually adopt, by
resolution, an appropriations limit each year for the following fiscal year.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-064 Establishing Appropriations Limit for FY 2021-
22
July 13, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
For fiscal year 2021-22, the City of Palmdale estimates that tax proceeds to be received,
as well as tax proceeds appropriated by the City Council, will, as in prior years, continue
to be under the legal limit. The City's appropriations limit for fiscal year 2021-22 is
established at $149,438,388, a 5.17 percent increase over the fiscal year 2020-21 limit.
This is the maximum amount of tax proceeds the City will be able to receive and
appropriate in the coming fiscal year. The City's appropriations subject to the limit for
fiscal year 2021-22 are estimated to be $76,626,221. Therefore, the City's fiscal year
2021-22 adopted budget appropriations subject to the limit are $69,812,167 less than
the appropriations limit.

FISCAL IMPACT
Resolution No. CC 2021-064 would increase the total annual appropriations limit from
$142,092,220 to $149,438,388.

ISSUE

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-059, continuing
the Proclamation of a Local Emergency resulting from Coronavirus Disease (COVID-
19)

BACKGROUND
ln December 2019, a new communicable disease, Coronavirus Disease (COVID-19), was
first detected in Wuhan City, Hubei Province, China. Since that time, it has spread globally
to over 122 countries, infecting more than 126,000 individuals and resulting in more than
4,614 deaths. Symptoms of the virus include fever, cough, and shortness of breath, and
infected individuals have experienced a range of outcomes, from mild sickness to severe
illness and death. This incident is being called the “COVID-19 outbreak.”

On January 31, 2020, the United States Secretary of Health and Human Services, Alex
M. Azar ll, declared a Public Health Emergency to aid the United States in responding to
COVID-19. This order was renewed on April 26, 2020.

On March 4, 2020, the State of California declared a State of Emergency to aid in the
prevention and mitigation of the effects of the COVID-19 outbreak. That same day, the
County of Los Angeles declared a State of Emergency to prevent the further spread of
COVID-19 throughout the County of Los Angeles. Since that time, the counties of Orange,
Santa Clara, San Diego, Sonoma, and San Francisco, along with the cities of Los
Angeles, Long Beach, and San Francisco have also declared local health emergencies.

On March 11,2020, the World Health Organization declared the COVID-19 outbreak
a pandemic, which means a global epidemic. That same day, there were a total of
twenty- eight (28) cases of COVID-19 in the County of Los Angeles and one (1)
reported death.

DISCUSSION
On March 11,2020, the City's Director of Emergency Services proclaimed the
existence of a local emergency within the City of Palmdale, pursuant to California
Government Code Section 8630 and Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.28.060.
Emergency proclamations issued by the Director of Emergency Services are valid for
only seven (7) days. The City Council reviewed and ratified Resolution No. CC 2020-
048 on March 17, 2020, ratifying the Director of Emergency Services' Proclamation
of a Local Emergency Resulting from Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19),
Resolution No. CC 2020-048 and authorizing the Director of Emergency Services to
continue to take appropriate measures to protect the public health, safety, and
welfare, and obtain emergency aid from other agencies.

The City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2020-049 on April 7, 2020 and
continued the state of emergency.

On June 2, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2020-057 continuing
the proclamation of a local emergency.

On August 4, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2020-088 continuing
the proclamation of a local emergency.

On October 6, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2020-104
continuing the proclamation of a local emergency.

On November 17, 2020, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2020-110
continuing the proclamation of a local emergency.

On January 12, 2021, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2021-001
continuing the proclamation of a local emergency.

On March 2, 2021, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2021-021 continuing
the proclamation of a local emergency.

On May 6, 2021, the City Council adopted Resolution No. CC 2021-050 continuing the
proclamation of a local emergency.

The local emergency will continue until terminated by the City Council. The City
Council’s ratification of the local emergency is valid for sixty (60) days, unless
extended by further City Council action.

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-063 a Resolution authorizing the submission of the
application for the 2021 Local Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (JAG)
Program.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-063 authorizing the submission of the application
  for the 2021 JAG grant.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any documents related to
  the application, acceptance, and implementation of the grant.

BACKGROUND

Since November 2005, the City has contracted two (2) additional motorcycle deputies,
bringing the total number of motorcycle deputies contracted with the Los Angeles
Sheriff’s Department to five (5). The two additional motor deputies have provided critical
services in traffic and crime deterrence.

Each year the City sets goals to help reduce overall collisions and incidents. In 2020,
collisions were reduced by 4%, Speed-related collisions were reduced by 4%, DUI/DWI
related collisions were reduced by 5% and the percentage of DUI/DWI collisions
involving an injury or fatality were reduced by 5%. The two grant deputies also issued
2,900 citations for hazardous violations, concentrating on the speed-related problem
areas throughout the City, particularly around school zones. A total of 113 non-
hazardous citations were also issued and 191 traffic related arrests were made.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Resolution No. CC 2021-063
Page 2

The deputies are also available to respond to calls for service and will work in
coordination with the City’s Neighborhood Services Department to identify high-risk
areas and other areas of concern, such as school zones and are also responsible for
conducting DUI/DWI checkpoints and neighborhood traffic operations to reduce speed.

There are ten (10) project identifiers associated with the project activities, which include:
alcohol testing, drugs, corrections, crime prevention, DWI, education, evaluation,
impaired driving, policing and traffic enforcement.

The two (2) motorcycle deputies partially funded through this grant, will help mitigate
increasing traffic incidents and provide timely response to citizen complaints. They will
also help ensure that collisions will continue to decrease, thereby maintaining traffic
safety and community safety as law enforcement priorities.

City staff will submit specific performance measure data as required under the award.
The City’s performance measures correlate to the goals, objectives and deliverables
identified in the grant solicitation.

The City proposes utilizing the 2021 Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Grant (JAG)
program allocation of $48,344 to continue to assist with the cost of these two motor
deputies.

FISCAL IMPACT
The 2021 JAG grant allocation of $48,344 will be utilized to continue funding two
motorcycle deputies in account 10125002-721836-1072. In addition, $1,450.32 of the
grant allocation will be set aside for required training. The general fund will fund the
remaining $445,615.32 for the cost of the two deputies.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-066, a Resolution of the City Council of the City
  of Palmdale Amending the Conflict-of-Interest Code of the City of Palmdale and
  Repealing Resolution No. CC 2020-013 in its Entirety.

BACKGROUND
The Political Reform Act of 1974 (Government Code Section 81000, et seq.), requires
the City of Palmdale to adopt a conflict-of-interest code. The Fair Political Practices
Commission (FPPC) has adopted a resolution (2 California Code of Resolutions Section
18730) that contains the terms of a standard conflict-of-interest code, which can be
incorporated by reference in an agency’s code.
In 2020, the City of Palmdale adopted its conflict-of-interest code through Resolution
No. CC 2020-013, incorporating the terms of 2 California Code of Regulations Section
18730 by reference along with an appendix setting out which employees, members, and
consultants are designated to which disclosure categories.
DISCUSSION
Upon a recent review, Staff has determined that the City of Palmdale’s conflict-of-
interest code is out of date and requires amendment. Notably, because of the recent
personnel changes made during the last calendar year, the conflict-of-interest code
requires amendment to address new positions that are required to be designated, revise
the titles of existing positions, and delete certain positions that have been abolished.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

Additionally, an amendment to the conflict-of-interest code is required to address
changes to the organizational structure of the City.
The proposed resolution (Resolution No. CC 2021-066) addresses these necessary
changes and would repeal and replace the current conflict-of-interest code, adopted by
Resolution No. CC 2020-013, in its entirety.
Accordingly, Staff recommends approval of Resolution No. CC 2021-066.
FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

  RESOLUTION NO. CC 2021-066

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE
  REPEALING AND RESTATING THE CONFLICT-OF-INTEREST CODE
  OF THE CITY OF PALMDALE

  WHEREAS, the City of Palmdale has adopted a conflict-of-interest code as
required by The Political Reform Act, Government Code Section 81000, et seq.; and

  WHEREAS, Government Code Section 87306 requires a local government
agency to review and make amendments to its conflict-of-interest code when new
positions are created or duties are changed to existing designated positions; and

  WHEREAS, Government Code Section 87307 allows a local government agency
to review and make amendments to its conflict-of-interest code at any time and upon its
own initiative; and

  WHEREAS, The City of Palmdale has reviewed its conflict-of-interest code and
determined that it requires amendment; and

  WHEREAS, The City of Palmdale desires to amend its conflict-of-interest code
by replacing its current conflict-of-interest code, adopted by Resolution CC 2020-013.

NOW THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
PALMDALE DOES HEREBY FIND, DETERMINE, RESOLVE AND ORDER AS
FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. Resolution CC 2020-013 is repealed in its entirety.

  SECTION 2. The Fair Political Practices Commission has adopted a Model
Conflict of Interest Code (“Model Code”). The Model Code, codified at 2 California
Code of Regulations Section 18730, can be incorporated by reference by the City as its
conflict-of-interest code. That Model Code will be amended by the Fair Political
Practices Commission from time to time to conform to amendments to the Political
Reform Act.

  SECTION 3. The Model Code, attached hereto and incorporated by reference
as Exhibit “A” and any amendments to it duly adopted by the Fair Political Practices
Commission, and Appendices A-G are hereby incorporated by reference and shall
constitute the conflict-of-interest code for the City of Palmdale for the following
departments:

§ 18730. Provisions of Conflict of Interest Codes.

  (a) Incorporation by reference of the terms of this regulation along with the designation

of employees and the formulation of disclosure categories in the Appendix referred to below

constitute the adoption and promulgation of a conflict of interest code within the meaning of

Section 87300 or the amendment of a conflict of interest code within the meaning of Section

87306 if the terms of this regulation are substituted for terms of a conflict of interest code

already in effect. A code so amended or adopted and promulgated requires the reporting of

reportable items in a manner substantially equivalent to the requirements of article 2 of chapter 7

of the Political Reform Act, Sections 81000, et seq. The requirements of a conflict of interest

code are in addition to other requirements of the Political Reform Act, such as the general

prohibition against conflicts of interest contained in Section 87100, and to other state or local

laws pertaining to conflicts of interest.

  (b) The terms of a conflict of interest code amended or adopted and promulgated pursuant

to this regulation are as follows:

  (1) Section 1. Definitions.

  The definitions contained in the Political Reform Act of 1974, regulations of the Fair

Political Practices Commission (Regulations 18110, et seq.), and any amendments to the Act or

regulations, are incorporated by reference into this conflict of interest code.

  (2) Section 2. Designated Employees.

  1
   The persons holding positions listed in the Appendix are designated employees. It has

been determined that these persons make or participate in the making of decisions which may

foreseeably have a material effect on economic interests.

  (3) Section 3. Disclosure Categories.

  This code does not establish any disclosure obligation for those designated employees

who are also specified in Section 87200 if they are designated in this code in that same capacity

or if the geographical jurisdiction of this agency is the same as or is wholly included within the

jurisdiction in which those persons must report their economic interests pursuant to article 2 of

chapter 7 of the Political Reform Act, Sections 87200, et seq.

In addition, this code does not establish any disclosure obligation for any designated employees

who are designated in a conflict of interest code for another agency, if all of the following apply:

  (A) The geographical jurisdiction of this agency is the same as or is wholly included

within the jurisdiction of the other agency;

  (B) The disclosure assigned in the code of the other agency is the same as that required

under article 2 of chapter 7 of the Political Reform Act, Section 87200; and

  (C) The filing officer is the same for both agencies.1

  Such persons are covered by this code for disqualification purposes only. With respect to

all other designated employees, the disclosure categories set forth in the Appendix specify which

kinds of economic interests are reportable. Such a designated employee shall disclose in his or

her statement of economic interests those economic interests he or she has which are of the kind

described in the disclosure categories to which he or she is assigned in the Appendix. It has been

determined that the economic interests set forth in a designated employee's disclosure categories

  2
 are the kinds of economic interests which he or she foreseeably can affect materially through the

conduct of his or her office.

  (4) Section 4. Statements of Economic Interests: Place of Filing.

  The code reviewing body shall instruct all designated employees within its code to file

statements of economic interests with the agency or with the code reviewing body, as provided

by the code reviewing body in the agency's conflict of interest code.2

  (5) Section 5. Statements of Economic Interests: Time of Filing.

  (A) Initial Statements. All designated employees employed by the agency on the effective

date of this code, as originally adopted, promulgated and approved by the code reviewing body,

shall file statements within 30 days after the effective date of this code. Thereafter, each person

already in a position when it is designated by an amendment to this code shall file an initial

statement within 30 days after the effective date of the amendment.

  (B) Assuming Office Statements. All persons assuming designated positions after the

effective date of this code shall file statements within 30 days after assuming the designated

positions, or if subject to State Senate confirmation, 30 days after being nominated or appointed.

  (C) Annual Statements. All designated employees shall file statements no later than April

1. If a person reports for military service as defined in the Servicemember's Civil Relief Act, the

deadline for the annual statement of economic interests is 30 days following his or her return to

office, provided the person, or someone authorized to represent the person's interests, notifies the

filing officer in writing prior to the applicable filing deadline that he or she is subject to that

federal statute and is unable to meet the applicable deadline, and provides the filing officer

verification of his or her military status.

  3
   (D) Leaving Office Statements. All persons who leave designated positions shall file

statements within 30 days after leaving office.

  (5.5) Section 5.5. Statements for Persons Who Resign Prior to Assuming Office.

  Any person who resigns within 12 months of initial appointment, or within 30 days of the

date of notice provided by the filing officer to file an assuming office statement, is not deemed to

have assumed office or left office, provided he or she did not make or participate in the making

of, or use his or her position to influence any decision and did not receive or become entitled to

receive any form of payment as a result of his or her appointment. Such persons shall not file

either an assuming or leaving office statement.

  (A) Any person who resigns a position within 30 days of the date of a notice from the

filing officer shall do both of the following:

  (1) File a written resignation with the appointing power; and

  (2) File a written statement with the filing officer declaring under penalty of perjury that

during the period between appointment and resignation he or she did not make, participate in the

making, or use the position to influence any decision of the agency or receive, or become entitled

to receive, any form of payment by virtue of being appointed to the position.

  (6) Section 6. Contents of and Period Covered by Statements of Economic Interests.

  (A) Contents of Initial Statements.

Initial statements shall disclose any reportable investments, interests in real property and

business positions held on the effective date of the code and income received during the 12

months prior to the effective date of the code.

  (B) Contents of Assuming Office Statements.

  4
   Assuming office statements shall disclose any reportable investments, interests in real

property and business positions held on the date of assuming office or, if subject to State Senate

confirmation or appointment, on the date of nomination, and income received during the 12

months prior to the date of assuming office or the date of being appointed or nominated,

respectively.

  (C) Contents of Annual Statements. Annual statements shall disclose any reportable

investments, interests in real property, income and business positions held or received during the

previous calendar year provided, however, that the period covered by an employee's first annual

statement shall begin on the effective date of the code or the date of assuming office whichever

is later, or for a board or commission member subject to Section 87302.6, the day after the

closing date of the most recent statement filed by the member pursuant to Regulation 18754.

  (D) Contents of Leaving Office Statements.

Leaving office statements shall disclose reportable investments, interests in real property, income

and business positions held or received during the period between the closing date of the last

statement filed and the date of leaving office.

  (7) Section 7. Manner of Reporting.

Statements of economic interests shall be made on forms prescribed by the Fair Political

Practices Commission and supplied by the agency, and shall contain the following information:

  (A) Investment and Real Property Disclosure.

When an investment or an interest in real property3 is required to be reported,4 the statement

shall contain the following:

  1. A statement of the nature of the investment or interest;

  5
   2. The name of the business entity in which each investment is held, and a general

description of the business activity in which the business entity is engaged;

  3. The address or other precise location of the real property;

  4. A statement whether the fair market value of the investment or interest in real property

equals or exceeds $2,000, exceeds $10,000, exceeds $100,000, or exceeds $1,000,000.

  (B) Personal Income Disclosure. When personal income is required to be reported,5 the

statement shall contain:

  1. The name and address of each source of income aggregating $500 or more in value, or

$50 or more in value if the income was a gift, and a general description of the business activity,

if any, of each source;

  2. A statement whether the aggregate value of income from each source, or in the case of

a loan, the highest amount owed to each source, was $1,000 or less, greater than $1,000, greater

than $10,000, or greater than $100,000;

  3. A description of the consideration, if any, for which the income was received;

  4. In the case of a gift, the name, address and business activity of the donor and any

intermediary through which the gift was made; a description of the gift; the amount or value of

the gift; and the date on which the gift was received;

  5. In the case of a loan, the annual interest rate and the security, if any, given for the loan

and the term of the loan.

  (C) Business Entity Income Disclosure. When income of a business entity, including

income of a sole proprietorship, is required to be reported,6 the statement shall contain:

  1. The name, address, and a general description of the business activity of the business

entity;

  6
   2. The name of every person from whom the business entity received payments if the

filer's pro rata share of gross receipts from such person was equal to or greater than $10,000.

  (D) Business Position Disclosure. When business positions are required to be reported, a

designated employee shall list the name and address of each business entity in which he or she is

a director, officer, partner, trustee, employee, or in which he or she holds any position of

management, a description of the business activity in which the business entity is engaged, and

the designated employee's position with the business entity.

  (E) Acquisition or Disposal During Reporting Period. In the case of an annual or leaving

office statement, if an investment or an interest in real property was partially or wholly acquired

or disposed of during the period covered by the statement, the statement shall contain the date of

acquisition or disposal.

  (8.3) Section 8.3. Loan Terms.

  (A) Except as set forth in subdivision (B), no elected officer of a state or local

  (8.4) Section 8.4. Personal Loans.

  (A) Except as set forth in subdivision (B), a personal loan received by any designated

employee shall become a gift to the designated employee for the purposes of this section in the

   (9) Section 9. Disqualification.

  No designated employee shall make, participate in making, or in any way attempt to use

his or her official position to influence the making of any governmental decision which he or she

knows or has reason to know will have a reasonably foreseeable material financial effect,

distinguishable from its effect on the public generally, on the official or a member of his or her

immediate family or on:

  (A) Any business entity in which the designated employee has a direct or indirect

investment worth $2,000 or more;

  (B) Any real property in which the designated employee has a direct or indirect interest

worth $2,000 or more;

  (C) Any source of income, other than gifts and other than loans by a commercial lending

institution in the regular course of business on terms available to the public without regard to

official status, aggregating $500 or more in value provided to, received by or promised to the

designated employee within 12 months prior to the time when the decision is made;

  (D) Any business entity in which the designated employee is a director, officer, partner,

trustee, employee, or holds any position of management; or

  (E) Any donor of, or any intermediary or agent for a donor of, a gift or gifts aggregating

$500 or more provided to, received by, or promised to the designated employee within 12

months prior to the time when the decision is made.

  (9.3) Section 9.3. Legally Required Participation.

No designated employee shall be prevented from making or participating in the making of any

decision to the extent his or her participation is legally required for the decision to be made. The

  12
 fact that the vote of a designated employee who is on a voting body is needed to break a tie does

not make his or her participation legally required for purposes of this section.

  (9.5) Section 9.5. Disqualification of State Officers and Employees.

In addition to the general disqualification provisions of section 9, no state administrative official

shall make, participate in making, or use his or her official position to influence any

governmental decision directly relating to any contract where the state administrative official

knows or has reason to know that any party to the contract is a person with whom the state

administrative official, or any member of his or her immediate family has, within 12 months

prior to the time when the official action is to be taken:

  (A) Engaged in a business transaction or transactions on terms not available to members

of the public, regarding any investment or interest in real property; or

  (B) Engaged in a business transaction or transactions on terms not available to members

of the public regarding the rendering of goods or services totaling in value $1,000 or more.

  (10) Section 10. Disclosure of Disqualifying Interest.

  When a designated employee determines that he or she should not make a governmental

decision because he or she has a disqualifying interest in it, the determination not to act may be

accompanied by disclosure of the disqualifying interest.

  (11) Section 11. Assistance of the Commission and Counsel.

  Any designated employee who is unsure of his or her duties under this code may request

assistance from the Fair Political Practices Commission pursuant to Section 83114 and

Regulations 18329 and 18329.5 or from the attorney for his or her agency, provided that nothing

in this section requires the attorney for the agency to issue any formal or informal opinion.

ISSUE
Approve Agreement with Pacific Advanced Civil Engineering, Inc. (PACE) for engineering
design services on PN 788, the Palmdale Transportation Center Infrastructure Support
Project in the amount of $329,750.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-7429, with Pacific Advanced Civil Engineering, Inc.
  (PACE) for engineering design services on PN 788, the Palmdale Transportation
  Center Infrastructure Support Project.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-7429,
  with Pacific Advanced Civil Engineering, Inc. (PACE), including minimal and/or

BACKGROUND
In January 2021, the City Council approved Agreement A-7316, between the City of
Palmdale and the Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority (LACMTA)
in association with the Palmdale Transportation Center Infrastructure Support Project.
This agreement was in response to the LACMTA approval of the programming of
$2,000,000 in Measure “M” funds and established a scope of work that best serves the
Palmdale Transportation Center, the future multi modal high-speed rail, and the SR-138
Corridor as a whole. Agreement A-7429 authorizes the first of multiple projects to be
accomplished using these programmed funds.

DISCUSSION
The Palmdale Transportation Center Infrastructure Support Project will refine and expand
on the initial infrastructure analysis as identified by the California High Speed Rail
Authority (HSRA). It will include an analysis of the existing and future planned
infrastructure systems necessary to support the future multi modal high-speed rail,
Metrolink and BrightlineRailUSA Station, and may be used by the California High-Speed
Rail Authority to support the development of future design documents.

This phase of the project includes an environmental assessment and watershed
hydrology study of the Anaverde Creek Watershed. The current HSRA plan and
alignment places the proposed Station in a FEMA identified flood zone. HSRA has
prepared a draft Preliminary Engineering for Project Definition (PEPD) Report for the
FEMA Flood Hazard Evaluation and the Hydrology and Hydraulics of the Palmdale to
Burbank Section, which identify the need for a regional stormwater detention basin to
mitigate peak stormwater flows and alleviate the flood zone. These documents
recommend refinements be made to the existing watershed analysis, and although some
preliminary work has been performed by the City, more detailed analysis and refinement
of the watershed hydrology is necessary prior to proceeding with the design of the
regional detention basin.

This project will include design level hydrology for the Anaverde Creek Watershed and
will be guided by the Anaverde Watershed section of the City’s Master Plan of Drainage
(prepared by AKM Consulting Engineers on August 1996) and Lower Anaverde
Watershed Drainage Study (prepared by CDM Smith in June 2010). It will also assess
and accommodate the recommendations listed in the HSRA draft Hydrology and
Hydraulics Study, dated February 2019, and make specific recommendations regarding
the regional stormwater detention facilities.

The exhibit on the following page illustrates the flood area resulting from a simulated
rainfall event within the Anaverde Creek Watershed. Darker blue areas indicate deeper
flood depths. The successful completion of this project will result in a clear path and
strategy forward for mitigating stormwater runoff from Anaverde Creek, which will reduce
the indicated flood areas and open the region surrounding the Palmdale Transportation
Center to the potential of future development.

Palmdale.

  HIGHWAY AND 25TH STREET EAST, IN ASSOCIATION WITH A LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY PUBLIC WORKS COOPERATIVE PAVING
  PROJECT, IN THE AMOUNT OF $251,700.
ISSUE
Award Construction Contract with Hardy & Harper Inc. to provide additional pavement
overlay construction for Barrel Springs Road from 32nd Street East to the intersection of
Pearblossom Highway and 25th Street East, in association with a Los Angeles County
Public Works Cooperative Paving Project, in the amount of $251,700.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award Construction Contract with Hardy & Harper Inc. to provide additional
  pavement overlay construction for Barrel Springs Road from 32nd Street East to
  the intersection of Pearblossom Highway and 25th Street East, in association with
  a Los Angeles County Public Works Cooperative Paving Project, in the amount
  of $251,700; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. 7553 with
  Hardy & Harper Inc, including minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The City of Palmdale and Los Angeles County regularly cooperate on split jurisdiction
roadways and are working together on a cooperative pavement rehabilitation project
along Barrel Springs Road from the City Boundary to Cheseboro Road. The work
involved includes cold milling the existing pavement, applying an asphalt concrete
leveling course and then an asphalt rubber hot mix cap along with shoulder grading.
The City is responsible for half width of the roadway from 47th Street East to 32nd Street
East. The cost of this original work is approximately $250,000. Upon review of the
remaining portion of Barrel Springs Road that is solely in the City, it was determined that
 Report to Mayor and City Council

July 13, 2021

this street section is in equally poor condition and the most efficient approach to make
it better is to have this work done at the same time. The most efficient way to achieve
this is for the City to contract directly with Hardy & Harper Inc. to do the requested
additional work. Hardy and Harper Inc. would keep the same unit pricing that was
originally bid with the County, provide payment and performance bonds for the additional
work and construction would be continuous instead of stopping and starting a new
project.
DISCUSSION
Los Angeles County contracted the original scope with Hardy & Harper, Inc. under their
Job Order Contract (JOC) means and methods. Hardy & Harper, Inc. is a paving
contractor that works in the Southern California area and has worked for the City of
Palmdale completing the Rancho Vista Boulevard (30th West to 50th West) Resurfacing
project in 2017.

SUBJECT:  AWARD BID NO. 21-002-3600 TO SMITH PIPE & SUPPLY, INC. FOR
  IRRIGATION AND WATER CONSERVATION SUPPLIES IN AN
  AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $216,600.

ISSUE
Award Bid No. 21-002-3600 to Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc. for irrigation and water
conservation supplies in an amount not to exceed $216,000.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award of Bid No. 21-002-3600 to Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc. for irrigation water
  conservation supplies in an amount not to exceed $216,000.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee, to execute the purchase order with
  Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc including making minor and non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The Landscape Maintenance Section is responsible for materials for maintaining
irrigation system infrastructure in Parks, Landscape Maintenance Districts, General
Benefits, PTC, Park and Rides and Fairway Business Park landscapes. These supplies
are important for sustainable grounds and green spaces and water conservation efforts.
DISCUSSION
The City released Invitation for Bids (IFB) No. 21-002-3600 Irrigation and Water
Conservation Supplies on March 29, 2021. Notification of the IFB release was sent
electronically to 14 eligible vendors in the City’s PlanetBids vendor database for a period
of 30 days. One (1) vendor responded to the IFB and the bid proposal was evaluated
on a fixed unit price basis, lowest responsive bidder. Please note, that maintenance
staff did reach out to vendors during the bidding period to remind them about the project
bid. After only one bid received, staff again reached out to the vendors and received
one comment back stating that the vendor’s sales staff may have forgotten to submit.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

Pipe & Supply, Inc.

Village, CA) is summarized in the attached IFB No. 21-002-3600 Irrigation and Water
Conservation Supplies Bid Tabulation. Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc. has been supplying
irrigation material for the City for the past six (6) years.
Purchase Order No. 20220002 with Smith Pipe & Supply, Inc. resulting from the award
of IFB 21-002-3600 will be initially for a term of one (1) year (FY 2021-2022) July 1, 2021
through June 30, 2022. The City reserves the right and option to extend the term for two
(2) additional one (1) year periods upon mutual consent of the same terms and

ISSUE
Award Bid No. 21-002-3100, As-Needed Streetlight Pole Replacement and
Maintenance Services and approve Agreement between the City of Palmdale and M.
Brey Electric, Inc. in the amount of $150,000 per year or $450,000 for the three (3) year
term.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Award Bid No. 21-002-3100 As-Needed Streetlight Pole Replacement and
  Maintenance Services.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-7543
  between the City of Palmdale and M. Brey Electric, Inc. in the amount of $150,000
  per year or $450,000 for the three (3) year term.

BACKGROUND
The City of Palmdale Traffic Signal and Street Lighting Division is responsible for the
maintenance of approximately 18,000 street light poles that illuminate our citywide
roadway network. As part of maintenance, it is important to quickly respond when
replacing any damaged street light poles due to knock downs as a result of a collision. It
is necessary to have a contractor readily available to conduct pole repairs in a timely
manner.

DISCUSSION
The City released Invitation for Bids (IFB) No. 21-002-3100 As-Needed Streetlight Poles
Replacement and Maintenance Services on April 12, 2021. Two (2) vendors responded

conditions with the vendor.

services on PN 826, the Palmdale Regional Recreation Complex Project in the amount
of $307,485.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement No. A-7541, with Barker Rinker Seacat Architecture for
  engineering design services on PN 826, the Palmdale Regional Recreation
  Complex Project.

  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute Agreement No. A-7541,
  with Barker Rinker Seacat Architecture, including minimal and/or non-substantive
  changes.

BACKGROUND
In May 2021, at the Joint Palmdale and Lancaster City Council meeting, Agenda Item 7.2
for the Antelope Valley Event & Evacuation Center in Lancaster, and Regional Recreation
Complex in Palmdale, was unanimously approved.

The City of Lancaster and the City of Palmdale have identified the need for a new, larger,
Event Center that, with certain facility upgrades, may also serve as a Regional Evacuation
Center for the Antelope Valley, as well as a Regional Recreation Complex that provides
a multi-generational place of entertainment for the Antelope Valley. Working together the
Cities will expeditiously and efficiently identify a location, finance, and oversee the
process of environmental review, design, bid, and construction of each project to their
respective completion.
 Report to Mayor and City Council

July 13, 2021
Page 2

DISCUSSION
The Palmdale Regional Recreation Complex will be a state-of-the-art ±100,000 square
foot facility that enhances the quality of life, provides economic development
opportunities, and improves the health of its community residents. It will offer indoor, year-
round opportunities for social interaction, learning, fun, and fitness all in one location, and
provide services that meet the current trends and interests of its community. These trends
will ultimately be identified through community outreach, but may include the following:

1. Sports and physical activities serving a variety of ages, such as a multi-sport indoor
  gymnasium, multi-sport indoor synthetic turf fields, multi-sport outdoor synthetic turf
  fields, and an indoor walking track.
2. General recreation programming and rentals, such as multi-purpose rooms with
  removable dividers and automated presentation equipment or a fitness room with
  appropriate flooring.
3. Diverse recreational amenities such as a rock wall, boxing ring, pump bicycle track,
  handball courts, racquetball courts, and pickleball courts.
4. The potential to extend library services to serve youth needing educational support,
  including computer workstations, a small collection of books, space for small
  informational seminars, or office/meeting space for local non-profits and schools to
  provide needed youth services.
5. Unique elements to create local excitement and build community pride, such as a
  playground geared towards those with cognitive or physical limitations, an indoor
  warm water therapy pool, an indoor cool water exercise pool, or exciting water
  activities such as a wave rider or wave pool.
6. Outdoor amenities such as tiered grass seating for small bands and neighborhood
  events, or a drive-in movie set-up.
7. Expansive offering of indoor exercise equipment, complete with full-service locker
  rooms and space to hold common group fitness classes.

The scope of work for this project includes the professional services necessary to prepare
a feasibility study and conceptual plan for the Regional Recreation Complex in the City of
Palmdale, and can be categorized into four main categories, as outlined below:

1. Community outreach – Engage public opinion through community workshops,
  surveys, and social medial advertising.
2. Site analysis and selection – Analyze potential sites for the Regional Recreation
  Complex and provide three site selection recommendations.
3. Conceptual design – Design a conceptual building and site play layout, incorporating
  amenities as indicated in the results of the community outreach.
4. Probable construction cost and pro forma analysis – Prepare a probable construction
  cost for each of the three site selection recommendations, and a perform a pro forma
  analysis to project potential revenue.

such as SketchUp or AutoCAD Revit.

magnitude (ROM) costs for the major components of the project, including building,
on-site improvements, off-site improvements, utility infrastructure, right of way
acquisition, and any other major cost categories identified by the Consultant. Results
shall be organized and presented in a table for each site and shall be relied upon as a
reference when selecting the final site location.

  Additional Joint City Council discussion between the City of Lancaster, City of
  Palmdale, Supervisor Barger, and staff included the great overall impact of
  both cities working together and having a united front.

  City of Lancaster City Council took action to approve JNB 7.6 as presented.

  On a motion by Council Member Loa, and seconded by Mayor Pro Tem
  Bettencourt, the City Council 1. Directed staff to draft guiding principles that
  foster regional collaboration and transparency on business attraction,
  expansion, and retention efforts; and 2. Directed staff to explore potential
  funding options to support future economic development initiatives that benefit
  the region, by the following vote: 4-0-0-0; AYES: Hofbauer, Bettencourt,
  Carrillo, Loa; NOES: None; ABSTAIN: None; ABSENT: None

 8.  CLOSING COMMENTS BY CITY COUNCIL MEMBERS

  Joint City Council discussion between the City of Lancaster, City of Palmdale,
  Supervisor Barger, and staff included the future of additional joint meetings to keep the
  discussions going, and the impact of having two City Managers leading each of their
  cities in the right direction.

  Supervisor Barger thanked each city on behalf of her staff for everything each city does
  to help them do their job in the county better, and indicated leaders do lead, and
  discussed the hard work ahead, her appreciation for the leadership in the Antelope
  Valley, the forward movement of this agenda, and the exciting time for the Antelope
  Valley.

  Mayor Parris thanked the college for hosting the Joint Council Meeting, AV Edge for
  their assistance with handling the COVID situation, and the City of Palmdale, and
  discussed his support of the collaborative efforts of both cities.

  Additionally, Supervisor Barger discussed taking the time to thank the law enforcement
  for the jobs they do each and every day including their dedication and service to the
  community.

  City of Palmdale Mayor Hofbauer discussed an upcoming law enforcement event.

ISSUE
Shall the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-069 Amending the City’s
Classification and Pay Plan for Bargaining Unit Positions?

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. CC 2021-069 Amending
the City’s Classification and Pay Plan for Bargaining Unit Positions.

BACKGROUND
The Human Resources Division monitors and evaluates positions within the organization
and makes recommendations based on the needs of the City.

DISCUSSION

At the June 15, 2021 City Council meeting, the Fiscal Year 2021-22 budget was approved.
As a result, the City’s Classification and Pay Plan for Bargaining Unit Positions has been
updated and requires City Council approval.

In addition, the California Public Employees’ Retirement System (CalPERS) requires the
City to approve Classification and Pay Plans separately, not in combination with other
items on the agenda, such as the budget. To comply with CalPERS guidelines, staff is
submitting the Classification and Pay Plan for Bargaining Unit positions for approval.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with this action.

SUBJECT:  APPROVE REAPPOINTMENTS AND APPOINTMENT TO FILL A
  VACANCY ON THE MOBILE HOME PARK RENTAL REVIEW
  BOARD

ISSUE
Approve reappointments and an appointment to fill a vacancy on the Mobile Home Park
Rental Review Board.

RECOMMENDATION
Pursuant to the Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.080.030 staff recommends the
following:

  1. Approve the reappointment of Joan Ferry-Scott and Debra McLaurin to serve as
  Board Member of the Mobile Home Park Rental Review Board for a two-year
  term to expire on June 30, 2023.
  2. Approve the appointment of Eduardo De Santiago to fill a vacancy on the Mobile
  Home Park Rental Review Board for a two-year term to expire on June 30, 2023.

BACKGROUND
The Mobile Home Park Rental Review Board (“Board”) consists of five (5) members. No
member of the Board shall be a resident or owner of a mobile home park or an employee
of a park owner; and no member shall have a financial interest (as defined by state law)
in any mobile home or mobile home park, or have a parent, child, spouse or sibling with
any such financial interest. Prior to his/her appointment to the Board, each member shall
file a declaration to this effect with the City Clerk. As defined in Palmdale Municipal Code
Section 5.44.030, Board members must have an ability to attend meetings, and have a
basic knowledge of the guidelines of the Mobile Home Space Rent Control, Section 5.44
of the Palmdale Municipal Code. Applicants should also possess a fundamental
knowledge of business accounting (receivables, depreciation, capital expenditures, profit,
and loss statements, etc.).
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Approval of Reappointments to Mobile Home Park Rental Review Board
July 13, 2021
Page 2

All members shall be residents of the City. All members of the Board serve at the
pleasure of the City Council, and any member may be removed, with or without cause,
by a majority vote of the City Council. Board members serve a two-year term.

DISCUSSION
The terms of the current Mobile Home Park Rental Review Board members, Joan Ferry-
Scott, and Debra McLaurin expired on June 30, 2021. Each of whom have expressed
intent to continue to serve the City Council in this capacity.

In addition, due to the resignation of an existing Board member in early February 2021,
staff conducted a recruitment to fill the vacancy and advertised for the position in the A.V.
Press Classified ads. The job posting, including the duties and responsibilities were
published on the City’s website. A press release was also prepared by the
Communications Department and made available to the public. A total of six (6)
applications were received. After review and consideration of applications and letters of
interest in reappointment, Ms. Joan Ferry-Scott and Debra McLaurin have been
nominated for reappointment and Eduardo De Santiago for appointment, all for a two-
year term to expire on June 30, 2023.

Although the annual meetings are held in February each year, the reappointments and
vacancies must be filled in the event of a special rent increase, which would trigger a
special board meeting.

FISCAL IMPACT
Board members receive $100 per meeting and the Chair receives $150 per meeting.
Approximately $2,500.00 was needed for advertising.

ISSUE

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends pursuant to the Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.080.030 that the
City Council approve the reappointment of the Public Member to the City of Palmdale
Audit Committee for a as follows:

  1. Reappoint Christine Geary to serve as the Public Member of the Palmdale Audit
  Committee for a two-year term.

BACKGROUND
The purpose of the City of Palmdale Audit Committee (“Committee”) is to facilitate
communication between the auditor of the City’s financial statements and the City Council
and City management staff. The goal of the Audit Committee is to maintain the public’s
confidence in the City’s finance functions, enhance the accessibility of the City’s financial
matters to our citizens, and promote the financial transparency of the City.

Per PMC 3.05.030 Composition, qualifications, and compensation.
  (A) The City of Palmdale Audit Committee shall consist of five members,
  comprised as follows:
  (1) Two members from the City Council;
  (2) The City Manager;
  (3) The Director of Finance; and
  (4) One member from the public.
  (B) The public member of the City of Palmdale Audit Committee shall be appointed
  by, and serve at the pleasure of, the City Council.
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Reappointment of City of Palmdale Audit Committee Public Member
July 13, 2021
Page 2

  (C) The public member shall have some expertise in accounting, auditing, financial
  reporting, and internal controls. Ideally, the public member would be a certified
  public accountant. Residency within the city of Palmdale is desired but not
  required.
  (D) Members of the City of Palmdale Audit Committee shall not receive
  compensation nor be eligible for reimbursement. (Ord. 1434 § 1, 2012)

The City of Palmdale Audit Committee generally convenes each year in the spring and
fall in the City Council Chamber located at 38300 Sierra Highway, Suite B, Palmdale,
California.

DISCUSSION
In November 2020, Ms. Christine Geary was appointed to the Committee to fill a vacancy
which had become available due to the resignation of a long-standing Committee
member. After a lengthy recruitment and review of qualified applicants, Ms. Geary was
nominated to fill the vacancy until the term expired earlier this year in January. Ms. Geary
has expressed her interest, as well as and her intent to continue to serve the City Council
in this capacity.

FISCAL IMPACT
There is no fiscal impact associated with the appointment of a member of the public to
the audit committee. This position does not receive compensation for their service.

 SUBJECT:  INFORMATION ITEM: CITY OF PALMDALE PROSECUTIONS

ISSUE
Receive information regarding prosecutions within the City of Palmdale.

RECOMMENDATION
Receive information and file.

BACKGROUND
At the City Council meeting on June 22, 2021, the Council directed staff to return with an
update on a previous inquiry regarding functions of the City Attorney as the City
Prosecutor and current state of prosecutions in the City of Palmdale. This report will
provide an update to the previous report.

Generally, the office of the District Attorney of the respective county within which a city
resides is responsible for the prosecution of all state law misdemeanors committed within
the jurisdiction. (Gov. Code § 26500).

At present, the City Attorney’s office has significant prosecutorial authority to prosecute
violations of the Palmdale Municipal Code and Ordinances. Palmdale Municipal Code
section 2.06.060 provides this authority; “(Powers and Duties) provides the following:
“The City Attorney shall have the following powers and duties…(b) to initiate all
proceedings in law or equity for the criminal or civil enforcement of all City ordinances
and for the defense of the City in all legal actions.” These violations can be charged, or
filed, as administrative actions, infractions, or misdemeanors. The associated penalty for

ISSUE
Adopt ORDINANCE NO. 1565 approving Zoning Ordinance Amendment (ZOA) 21-002
amending Sections 17.16 (Definitions), 17.26.040 (Minor Modifications to Approved
Plans), 17.95.040 (Communication Facilities), 17.95.05 (Wireless Telecommunication
Facilities in the Public Right-of-Way) and to add Section 17.95.060 (Emergency Standby
Generators) of Palmdale Municipal Code (PMC) Title 17 Zoning (Zoning Code) to
update the standards for the permitting, development, siting, installation, aesthetics,
design, operation and maintenance of wireless telecommunication facilities and to
provide for the installation of Emergency Standby Generators in compliance with State
and Federal requirements.

RECOMMENDATION
The Planning Commission recommends that the City Council adopt ORDINANCE NO.
1565 approving ZOA 21-002 amending Sections 17.16 (Definitions), 17.26.040 (Minor
Modifications to Approved Plans), 17.95.040 (Communication Facilities), 17.95.05
(Wireless Telecommunication Facilities in the Public Right-of-Way) and to add Section
17.95.060 (Emergency Standby Generators) of the PMC Zoning Code to update the
standards for the permitting, development, siting, installation, aesthetics, design,
operation and maintenance of wireless telecommunication facilities and to provide for
 Report to Mayor and City Council

the installation of Emergency Standby Generators in compliance with State and Federal
requirements.

BACKGROUND
In addition to achieving the primary goal of bringing the PMC into compliance with State
and Federal regulations regarding Wireless Telecommunications Facilities, ZOA 21-002
also provides the opportunity to address requirements for eligible facilities and to refine
regulations regarding Wireless Telecommunications Facilities located both on public and
private property. Furthermore, ZOA 21-002 will improve the convenience for users of the
Zoning Code, including applicants, staff, wireless service providers and the general
public, by creating a more streamlined, and internally consistent document.

Staff considered the needs of the public as well as practical zoning and physical
requirements and worked closely with several wireless telecommunication service
providers to craft an ordinance that addresses the various needs of all parties. Staff
coordinated with the providers over several months. This coordination resulted in
revisions and refining of the ordinance. After public circulation of the draft Ordinance,
but prior to the Planning Commission hearing, at the request of Verizon, Crown Castle
and T-Mobile additional revisions to the ordinance were made. On May 13, 2021, a draft
Ordinance was presented to the Planning Commission. Shortly before the Planning
Commission hearing additional comments were received from Verizon’s legal counsel.
The Planning Commission unanimously recommended that the City Council approve
the subject ZOA, as amended. As part of the motion to recommend approval of ZOA
21-002 by the City Council, the Planning Commission directed staff to review the letter
provided by Verizon’s counsel and recommend that any appropriate response or
revisions be presented to the City Council for their consideration with the ZOA. As a
result of this subsequent review, an additional change has been made to the ordinance
to further facilitate wireless installations within the public right-of-way.

FISCAL IMPACT
ZOA 21-002 would amend various sections of the Zoning Code in order to comply with
State and Federal regulations and clarify processes for the installation of Wireless
Telecommunication Facilities.  It is anticipated that ZOA 21-002 will have an
immeasurable net positive fiscal impact resulting from applications associated with new
and expanded Wireless Telecommunication Facilities.

Division 95.050 Wireless Telecommunications Facilities In The Public Right-Of-Way
17.95.050.010 Purpose and Intent
The purpose and intent of this Chapter is to provide a uniform and comprehensive set of
regulations and standards for the permitting, development, siting, installation, aesthetics,
design, operation and maintenance of wireless telecommunications facilities in the City’s
public right-of-way. These regulations are intended to establish and enforce aesthetic
standards consistent with the City’s authority to do so under Article XI section 7 of the
California Constitution and Public Utilities Code sections 7901 and 7901.1. This Section
is also intended to prescribe clear and reasonable criteria to assess and process
applications in a consistent and expeditious manner, while reducing the impacts
associated with wireless telecommunications facilities. This Chapter provides standards
necessary (A) for the preservation of the public right-of-way in the City for the maximum
benefit and use of the public, (B) to promote and protect public health and safety,
community welfare, visual resources and the aesthetic quality of the City consistent with
the goals, objectives and policies of the General Plan, and (C) to provide for the orderly,
managed and efficient development of wireless telecommunications facilities in
accordance with the State and Federal laws, rules and regulations.

A. Design and Development Standards. All wireless telecommunications facilities that
are located within the public right-of-way shall be designed and maintained as to minimize
visual, noise and other impacts on the surrounding community and shall be planned,
designed, located, and erected in accordance with the following:

A.1.  General Guidelines.

  a. 1. The applicant shall employ screening, undergrounding and
  stealthing/camouflage design techniques in the design and placement of wireless
  telecommunications facilities to ensure that the facility is as visually screened as
  feasible, to prevent the facility from dominating the surroundings.

  b. 2. To the maximum extent feasible, stealthing/camouflage designs shall be used
  in an effort to eliminate the need to screen such facilities such that landscaping
  would need to be removed. If screening is nevertheless required, the screening
  Screening shall be designed to be architecturally compatible with surrounding
  structures using appropriate techniques to camouflage, disguise, and/or blend into
  the environment, including landscaping, color, and other techniques to minimize the
  facility’s visual impact as well as be compatible with the architectural character of
  the surrounding buildings or structures in terms of color, size, proportion, style, and
  quality.

  c. 3. To the extent feasible, facilities shall be located such that views from a
  residential structure are not significantly impaired.

  2.  Reserved.

3. B. Traffic Safety. All facilities shall be designed and located in such a manner to avoid
adverse impacts on traffic safety. Among other things, when determining traffic safety
impacts, the City will consider the views of the Manual for Uniform Traffic Control Devices
(MUTCD) and whether the proposed installation location is high enough and far enough
away from the street to minimize the risk of high profile vehicles colliding with the
installation.

4. C. Blending Methods. All facilities shall have subdued colors and nonreflective
materials that blend with the materials and colors of the surrounding area and structures.

5. D. Equipment. The applicant shall use the least visible equipment possible. Antenna
elements shall be flush-mounted, to the extent feasible. All antenna mounts shall be
designed so as not to preclude possible future collocation by the same or other operators

standards outlined in this Section, all facilities shall be subject to the following conditions

  1. a. Identity, including the name, address and twenty-four (24) hour local or toll
  free contact phone number of the permittee, the owner, the operator, and the agent

  2. b.  The legal status of the owner of the communication facility.

A. Federal Law – Planning Commission Exception. The City Council recognizes that
Federal law prohibits a permit denial when it would effectively prohibit the provision of
personal wireless services and the applicant proposes the least intrusive means to
provide such services. The City Council finds that, due to wide variation among wireless
facilities, technical service objectives and changed circumstances over time, it is
appropriate to allow a limited exemption for proposals in which strict compliance with this
Chapter would effectively prohibit personal wireless services serves the public interest.
The City Council further finds that circumstances in which an effective prohibition may
occur are extremely difficult to discern, and that specified findings to guide the analysis
promotes clarity and the City’s legitimate interest in well-planned wireless facilities
deployment. Therefore, if any applicant demonstrates that strict compliance with any
provision in this Chapter, as applied to a specific proposed personal wireless services
facility, would effectively prohibit the provision of personal wireless services, the Planning
Commission may grant a limited, one (1) time exemption from strict compliance with the
requirements of this Code subject to the provisions in this Section.

B. Required Findings. The Planning Commission shall not grant any exception unless
the applicant demonstrates by a preponderance of the evidence all the following:

  1. The proposed wireless facility qualifies as a “personal wireless services facility”
  as defined in United States Code, Title 47, Section 332(c)(7)(C)(ii);

  2. 1. The applicant has provided the City with a clearly defined technical service
  objective and a clearly defined potential site search area;

  3. 2. The applicant has provided the City with a meaningful comparative analysis
  that includes the factual reasons why denial of the application would materially
  inhibit the deployment of personal wireless services. Such analysis shall include
  analysis of any alternative location(s) or design(s) suggested by the City or
  otherwise identified in the administrative record, including but not limited to potential
  alternatives identified at any public meeting or hearing, are not and an indication of
  whether such alternatives are technically feasible or potentially available; and

  4. 3. The applicant has provided the City with a meaningful comparative analysis
  that includes the factual reasons why the proposed location and design deviations
  are the least noncompliant location and design necessary to reasonably achieve the
  applicant’s reasonable technical service objectives.

C. Scope. The Planning Commission shall limit its exemption to the extent to which the
applicant demonstrates such exemption is necessary to reasonably achieve its

of approval as reasonably necessary to promote the purposes in this Chapter and protect

ISSUE
Shall the City Council approve Ordinance No. 1568 amending Section 2.04.060 of the
Palmdale Municipal Code to be consistent with Section 2.10.010 of the Palmdale
Municipal Code and the intent of Ordinance No. 1407 (2010)?

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Receive public testimony regarding Proposed Ordinance No. 1568; and
  2. Adopt Proposed Ordinance No. 1568.

BACKGROUND
Prior to 2010, the City Clerk was appointed by the City Council. On September 1, 2010,
the City Council passed Ordinance No. 1407 authorizing the City Manager, pursuant to
California Government Code §34856, to appoint the City Clerk, and amending Palmdale
Municipal Code Section 2.10.010 to effectuate this change. However, Ordinance No.
1407 did not make changes to Palmdale Municipal Code Section 2.04.060 relating to
the powers and duties of the City Manager. As such, the two municipal code sections
are inconsistent and in conflict regarding the City Manager’s authority to appoint,
manage, and remove the City Clerk.

DISCUSSION
Proposed Ordinance No. 1568 would make changes to Palmdale Municipal Code
Section 2.04.060 relating to the powers and duties of the City Manager to be consistent

  Background

basins throughout the City. In order to fund the maintenance of these projects and improvements, the City
has formed two Drainage Benefit Assessment Districts covering an area of approximately 6,600 acres and
approximately 1,470 parcels. The Districts have been formed and the levies have been made pursuant to
Section 54703 et seq. of the California Government Code, commonly known as the Benefit Assessment Act
of 1982, and Article XIII D of the California Constitution (the “Article XIII D”).
Drainage Benefit Assessment District No. 1 (“DBAD No. 1”) (Anaverde Master Planned Community Avenue
S at Approximately 20th Street West) is located within the Anaverde Master Planned Community at Avenue
S and approximately 20th Street West. Drainage Benefit Assessment District No. 2006-02 (“DBAD No.
2006-02) (Ritter Ranch Master Planned Community, Phase I through phase V, South of Elizabeth Lake Road
at Approximately 40th Street West) is located within the Ritter Ranch Master Planned Community along
Elizabeth Lake Road and west of the Anaverde Community.

  Process for Annual Assessment
In each subsequent year for which the assessment will be continued, the City Council may direct an
Engineer’s Report to be prepared on an annual basis which contains a full and detailed description of the
improvements, the boundaries of the assessment district and any zones therein, and the proposed
assessments upon assessable lots and parcels of land within the Districts.
The City Council may also annually adopt a resolution of intention which:
    Declares the intention of the City Council to levy and collect assessments within the assessment
  district for the fiscal year stated therein.

    Generally describes the existing and proposed improvements and any substantial changes
  proposed to be made in existing improvements.

    Refers to the report of the engineer, on file with the City Clerk, for a full and detailed description of
  the improvements, the boundaries of the assessment district and any zones therein, and the
  proposed assessments upon assessable lots and parcels of land within the district.

    Gives notice of the time and place for public hearing by the City Council on the levy of the
